paper.title: Accelerating materials property prediction via a hybrid Transformer Graph framework that leverages four body interactions
paper.research_summary: We propose a framework utilizing a Graph Neural Network with composition-based and crystal structure-based architectures, combined with a transfer learning scheme. This approach accurately predicts energy-related properties (e.g., total energy, energy above the convex hull, energy band gap) and data-scarce mechanical properties (e.g., bulk and shear modulus). Our model incorporates four-body interactions, capturing periodicity and structural characteristics. It outperforms state-of-the-art models in 8 materials property regression tasks.

task.objective: Accurately predict energy-related and mechanical properties of inorganic materials
constraints: capturing global crystal structure and periodicity
output_goal: predicted property values for energy-related and mechanical properties

evidence.text: This approach accurately predicts energy-related properties (e.g., total energy, energy above the convex hull, energy band gap) and data-scarce mechanical properties (e.g., bulk and shear modulus).

stages.stage_name_raw: using computational data from the MP21 public database
stages.stage_goal: Acquire computational data for training and testing

evidence.text: As training data, we used computational data from the MP21 public database4.

stages.stage_goal: Convert crystal structures into graph representations for model input

evidence.text: To convert a crystal structure into a graph representation, we employ a unique approach aimed at encapsulating the essential structural characteristics while minimizing the computational complexity.

stages.stage_goal: Train the hybrid CrysGNN and CoTAN model on material properties

evidence.text: The whole model is trained in a single hybrid manner to consider the effect of compositional properties and structure-properties relations simultaneously (hybrid CrysGNN and CoTAN: CrysCo).

stages.stage_goal: Fine-tune pre-trained models on data-scarce mechanical properties
stage_input: pre-trained models on primary properties (Ef, Eg, EHull)

evidence.text: To overcome the challenge of data scarcity, we employed TL techniques to leverage existing knowledge and enhance the performance of our model. By pretraining the model on a large-scale dataset of DFT computed formation energies, we were able to leverage the learned representations and fine-tune the model (CrysCoT).

stages.stage_goal: Evaluate model performance against state-of-the-art baselines
stage_input: state-of-the-art models (MEGNet, CGCNN, SchNet, ALIGNN, Matformer, DeeperGATGNN)

evidence.text: To benchmark CrysCo’s performance, we used 8 properties datasets (Table 1) that include material compositions, crystal structures, and tabulated physical and chemical descriptors as inputs.

stages.stage_name_raw: ablation study on number of EGAT layers
stages.stage_goal: Determine optimal number of EGAT layers for accuracy and computational efficiency

evidence.text: In order to determine the optimal balance between the accuracy and computational efficiency of CrysCo, we carried out an ablation study by changing the number of EGAT layers on the formation energy (Ef) prediction task.
